lessons.title: The Gym vs The Real World
lessons.content_md:
# Training vs Inference 🏋️‍♂️

Building an AI happens in two completely separate phases. Confusing them is one of the most common beginner mistakes.

## Phase 1: Training (Going to the Gym)

Imagine an athlete preparing for the Olympics. They spend months in the gym lifting weights, running drills, failing, adjusting their technique, and trying again. It takes massive amounts of time, energy, and sweat.

In AI, this is called **Training**. We feed the massive dataset into the empty neural network. The network makes guesses, gets them wrong, adjusts the "weights" (the math) between its neurons, and tries again. 

Training a massive AI model like ChatGPT can take months and cost tens of millions of dollars in electricity and supercomputer time.

<flipcard front="🏋️‍♂️ What is Training?" back="The intensive phase where the AI learns from data. It requires massive computing power to calculate and adjust the internal math of the network."></flipcard>

## Phase 2: Inference (Playing the Game)

Once the athlete goes to the Olympics, they aren't lifting weights anymore. They are taking all that built-up muscle and *using* it in the real world to win the race. It happens in seconds.

In AI, this is called **Inference**.

Once the network is trained, we freeze the math. When you ask ChatGPT a question on your phone, it isn't "learning" anything new. It's just taking your question and running it through the pre-calculated math to give you an answer instantly.

<flipcard front="🏃‍♂️ What is Inference?" back="Using a fully trained AI model to make predictions on new, unseen data. It is fast and requires very little computing power compared to training."></flipcard>

<flipcard front="📱 Can you run Inference on a phone?" back="Yes! Because inference just requires running data through frozen math equations, many AI models can run directly on your smartphone."></flipcard>
